tag: Episode 2 · A Cat in a Hat? Yeongnyangi
title: A Cat in a Hat? Yeongnyangi

beats.t: The lotus-leaf boat touched the landing on the Island of Companions. Tap. A smaller sound than Yeoni had expected.
The black hands pursuing them stopped abruptly at the island. They writhed outside the mist for a moment, then slipped beneath the river.
Clinging to the leaf's edge, Yeoni took a long time to catch their breath. Their short, fingerless forelegs were rigid with effort. Somehow, though, they were still holding on.
I'm alive...
A little snort slipped out after the words. Oink. Yeoni immediately clamped a hoof over their mouth.
No. That was just breathing. Not a pig noise.
Without answering, Yeongnyangi leaped lightly onto the landing. As his small body touched down, golden paw prints bloomed briefly on the black glass floor, then faded.
Wow. Add a few sound effects and this would be a whole game.
You still think this is a game?
Haven't given up hope. Give me one loading screen and I'll believe it immediately.
I understand that you're trying to find some other explanation.
I'll take that as a compliment. But seriously, what are you? A cat in a hat, or a cat doing cosplay?
...Not an ordinary cat.
Except you keep looking like a cat.
Say that once more and I'll leave those paw prints on your forehead.
Yes, yes, Lord Cat. Lord Cat of the Magnificent Hat.
Yeoni cautiously tried to climb off the leaf. Front hooves down first; then, as they shifted their hind legs—
Uh, whoa?
Their short legs refused to cooperate. Yeoni landed nose-first on the dock. Thud.
It did not hurt. Their pride hurt a little instead.
Your landing... could use some practice.
Stop analyzing me.
Isn't this the kind of thing that comes with a tutorial? No controls, no save function, not even a refund button.
A sharp snort punctuated the complaint. Oink. Its gravitas dropped by exactly half.
The Island of Companions was quiet. No grass, no houses, no people. Instead, the whole island seemed built from shards of mirrors.
The ground gleamed like black glass. Mirrors large and small floated in the air, some palm-sized, others as large as doors. Every one hung at a different angle.
Mirrors reflecting the sky. The river. The lotus-leaf boat. And mirrors reflecting Yeoni.
Yeoni peered into one nearby. A flower pig looked back. Pink body. Small flower perched on its head. Short forelegs.
It was far too cute. That was why Yeoni disliked it.
I still can't get used to this.
When did my cheeks get so chubby? Did someone secretly pump air into them?
Yeoni lifted a hoof; the flower pig in the mirror lifted one too, left and right reversed. Yeoni tilted their head; it tilted its head exactly the same way.
Hey. Stop copying me.
Naturally, the mirrored pig merely mouthed the words. No sound came out. Somehow that was even more irritating.
When Yeoni turned this way and that, their tail swayed along. That was cute too, which only made them more annoyed.
Come on, mess up just once. Give me a little lag and I'll admit you're fake.
Oh, seriously.
What's wrong?
My whole aesthetic was supposed to be cool and badass. Now someone's switched my genre to soothing animal cuteness.
...I can't tell whether you like it or hate it.
You wouldn't understand. Having your entire appearance change genres overnight.
I have been a finished masterpiece since birth.
Oh, yes. Of course you have.
Companion cat review: personality, two stars. But the hat's pretty, so... another half star. I'm being generous.
Yeoni let it go and walked farther inland. The mirror fragments grew denser as they went. But something was strange.
Some mirrors did not reflect Yeoni as a flower pig. At first, they thought they had imagined it. They stopped.
There was a person inside the mirror.
Wet hair. A loose hoodie. Sweatpants baggy at the knees. A charger cable tossed on the bed. A phone in one hand.
And a tired-looking, twenty-three-year-old college student staring down at the screen. Yeoni. The original Yeoni. So familiar it felt unfamiliar.
Yeoni approached the mirror slowly. Their hooves made little tapping sounds against the ground. Tap. Tap.

The Yeoni in the mirror sat on the bed, exactly as they had been in the real world moments before. Hair tied back carelessly, fatigue lingering on their face. Still, it was the face Yeoni knew as their own.
Human hands. Human legs. Human eyes. Everything Yeoni had lost was there, just one layer of glass away.
Yeoni looked down at their hooves, then back at the mirror. Something in their chest tightened strangely.
I... looked like that, didn't I?
The voice came out quieter than expected. Their throat kept closing.
Forgotten sensations returned all at once. Swiping across a screen with a finger. The hair tie resting around their wrist before they tied their hair.
The irritation of pulling off wet socks. The stunned emptiness of seeing their assignment disappear. All those tiny things had suddenly become impossibly distant.
Yeoni raised a hoof to the mirror. Cold. The reflected Yeoni raised a hand. Human palm and short hoof met with a single pane of glass between them.
An unexpected swell of emotion rose in Yeoni. They wanted to go back. They really did.
Until a moment ago, 'I want to go home' had been half a joke. Now it was different. The words had suddenly become real.
I want to go home. To my room. My bed. My fingers.
...Yeongnyangi.
I'm listening. Go on.
Is that... really me?
Yeongnyangi looked at the mirror. His expression grew a little more serious too.
Your original appearance.
Then if I go in there, can I go back?
No.
The answer was quick and firm. Unable to look away from the mirror, Yeoni asked again.
...Why?
The mirrors on the Island of Companions are not exits. They reflect the places you have lost.
Places?
The place you believed was yourself. The you others see. The you you wanted to become. And the places you feel you were pushed out of.
It sounded understandable, yet Yeoni did not want to understand. That made it worse.
Then the Yeoni in the mirror moved. Yeoni stopped breathing.
Until that moment, the mirror had clearly been copying them. Now it was the other way around.
The human Yeoni in the mirror wore a different expression. A little calmer. Standing a little straighter. A little more confident, in a way that did not feel like Yeoni at all.
You're late.
Yeoni froze.
...What?
You're always late.
Quiet words, sharp as fingernails. Without realizing it, Yeoni took a step back.
Late for your alarm. Late replying. Late apologizing. Late for every opportunity.
A thin crack appeared across the mirror.
And this time, too—you're late.
Yeoni bit their lip.
What are you?
Me? Yeoni.
That was the answer Yeoni hated most. They tapped their chest with a hoof.
I'm Yeoni.
Really? In that body?
For a moment, no words came. Yeoni was angry, but strangely unable to answer at once.
The Yeoni in the mirror was too natural. The appearance they had worn in their room. Their voice. Their face. Their expressions.
If someone had to choose the real Yeoni from the two of them, would they choose the pink flower pig? Or that person?
Be careful.
What is that thing?
A reflection created by the Island of Companions. A rival with your face. Another you, seeking your place.
So, a doppelgänger.
In simple terms, yes.
My life really is squeezing in every possible trope.
You are not here as a spectator.
There's no place for you here.
Those words echoed across the entire island. One by one, the surrounding mirrors began to shine. Each small mirror held a different scene.
The back row of a lecture hall. A seat someone else had already taken. Yeoni's message posted too late in the group-project chat. An unread reply.
A text canceling an interview. A contest entry that had failed to submit. And a single rice triangle lying on a convenience-store floor.
Hey, leave the rice triangle out of this. That's too pathetic.
Yeoni tossed it out like a joke, but their voice trembled at the end. Such little things. Individually, all of them could be laughed off.
But piled together, they made Yeoni feel constantly pushed aside. Nudged from their place, late, missing out—until eventually it felt as though they had ceased to exist.
Then the largest mirror slowly rose. It was different from the others. Dark blue light surrounded it, and its surface rippled like water.
A human Yeoni stood inside. This time, though, not in their room. Above a black river.
A tiny shoot had sprouted beneath that Yeoni's feet. Below the shoot, deep waters stirred.
[ 乙亥 ]
Yeoni stared quietly at the two characters appearing on the mirror's edge. Strangely, they could not look away.
Eulhae. They looked unfamiliar, like characters seen for the first time, yet felt like a name known long ago. Something rang softly inside Yeoni's chest. The flower on their head glowed faintly.
Found it.
Found what?
Your Day Pillar. The pillar of the day you were born. The characters closest to your center.
The Eulhae Day Pillar.
Eulhae...
As Yeoni said it, the flower shone a little brighter. The human Yeoni in the mirror saw the light too. For the first time, that face stiffened.
No.
The mirrored Yeoni reached out. The characters [乙亥] along the edge began sliding toward that outstretched hand.
Yeoni, stop it!
How!
Hold on to your name!
What does that mean! Explain it so I can understand!
Do not let your place be taken!
You hate yourself right now, don't you?
Yeoni hesitated.
You hate that body. You hate being here. You hate your real life and its rotten luck, too.
The reflected Yeoni stepped forward. The mirror's surface undulated like water.
So let me do it. I'm the real Yeoni.
Yeoni's heart plunged.
I'll go back in your place.
Yeoni could not breathe. That reflected self was all too convincing. Human form. Familiar face. Normal hands. Normal voice.
Everything the present Yeoni had lost, that other one possessed.
Even if you went home looking like that, nobody would believe you're you.
The words lodged in Yeoni's throat. They looked down at their hooves. Pink. Short and round. Cute, but nothing like themself.
Only for a moment. One very brief moment. What if that other one went back instead? What if that one was better?
The fact that they had thought it left Yeoni a little cold.
Do not listen too closely to those words.
But...
The mirror burrows into the gap where you dislike yourself.
Yeongnyangi stepped in front of Yeoni.
The Island of Companions is an island of conflict. But your opponent is not a stranger. It is another you, trying to take your place.
You talk too much.
The reflected Yeoni snapped their fingers. All the surrounding mirror fragments rose at once. Sharp glass rained toward Yeoni and Yeongnyangi.
Get back!
The golden tassel at the tip of Yeongnyangi's hat blazed. He leaped and spun in midair, golden claws striking away the glass. Clang. Clang. Clang.
Fragments scattered in every direction. The instant he landed, Yeongnyangi crouched again.
Keep your eyes on those characters!
Yeoni glared at the great mirror. Eulhae. The characters wavered between the human reflection and the flower pig, as though unable to choose their real owner.
You said they're mine.
Yes. They are the characters you must reclaim.
Then why are they trying to go over there?
Because you are denying yourself.
Yeoni held their breath. Denying reality. They had called it a dream. Insisted it was a game. Forced it into the shape of an otherworld adventure story.
They had kept rejecting the self that had become a flower pig. They could hardly help it. They did not want to admit it. They were frightened.
And little by little, the mirrored Yeoni had been occupying that gap.
Oh... Is that how it works?
The reflected Yeoni reached out again. The characters [乙亥] slid farther toward that hand. The flower on Yeoni's head wavered precariously.
Yeoni.
Yeoni closed their eyes. Just for a moment. A very brief moment. Then opened them again.
They were still afraid. Still wanted to go home. Still hated this body. Still wished this were a dream. But.
Hey.
The reflected Yeoni looked over. Yeoni tapped their chest with a hoof.
I don't like how I look right now either. Not one bit.
No fingers. Short legs. I oink when I get startled.
A tiny oink did indeed escape at the end.
...See? That annoys me too.
Exactly, so I can—
But.
Yeoni cut in. The flower shone again. Still weak, but clearer than before.
Even so, I'm Yeoni.
The reflected Yeoni's expression hardened.
Even looking like this.
Yeoni took a step forward. With such short legs, it was not a large step. But it was unmistakably forward.
Even if I was late.
Another step.
Even if things went wrong.
Another step.
Even if my luck has completely fallen apart.
At last, Yeoni stood before the great mirror.
I decide where I belong.
At that instant, the characters [乙亥] shuddered violently. The human Yeoni in the mirror clenched their teeth.
Not yet. You don't even know what you are.
The mirror cracked open. Dark blue water poured through the split. Deep, cold water. Within it, a tiny green shoot began to rise.
乙 — Eul.
Dark blue currents swirled beneath the shoot.
亥 — Hae.
Eul Wood. Hae Water. A small shoot and deep water. The mirrored characters finally revealed their full form.
[ 乙亥 ]
And then the human Yeoni took a step out of the mirror.
Yeoni froze. The human who had walked out smiled with a face exactly like their own.
Fine. Prove it, then.
Every mirror around them lit up at once.
Prove you're the real Yeoni.
Yeoni faced the opponent wearing their face. They had reclaimed nothing yet. But one thing was certain. Those characters, Eulhae, were the first pillar they had to take back.
Do not retreat.
Yeoni breathed in deeply. The small flower petals on their head stirred in the wind.
Right. But first, one thing.
The reflected Yeoni tilted their head. Yeoni narrowed their eyes.
Don't wear my face and smile like such a jerk.
The reflected Yeoni stopped smiling.
[ Island of Companions · The First Trial Begins ]
